splash.failed: Veydrop could not start its engine. Close the app and open it again.

errors.io: A file operation failed. Check that the disk is available and try again.
errors.permission_denied: Windows denied access to that location. Choose a folder you can write to.
errors.path_not_found: That file or folder no longer exists.
errors.port_in_use: That port is already used by another program. Choose another port in Settings.
errors.not_found: That item could not be found. It may have been removed.
errors.conflict: That action conflicts with the current state. Refresh and try again.
errors.unauthorized: This device is no longer signed in. Pair it again.
errors.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
errors.pairing_expired: The pairing code expired. Generate a new QR code.
errors.pairing_used: That pairing code was already used. Generate a new QR code.
errors.server_not_running: The transfer server is not running. Start it from Connect Device.
errors.no_network: No usable network connection was found.
errors.insufficient_space: There is not enough free disk space for this transfer.
errors.too_large: That file is larger than the limit set in Settings.
errors.hash_mismatch: The file arrived damaged: its checksum did not match, so it was discarded.
errors.offset_mismatch: The transfer lost sync and could not continue.
errors.zip_too_large: That selection is too large to download as a single ZIP. Download files individually.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.subtitle: Your PC, ready to exchange files with nearby phones.

empty.title: Nothing transferred yet
empty.desc: Connect a phone, then send or receive files. Completed transfers appear here.

connect.title: Connect Device
connect.subtitle: Scan the code with your phone's camera. No app needed.
connect.offDesc: Veydrop only listens on your network while you are connected. Nothing is exposed until you start.
connect.noNetwork: No usable network was found. Connect this PC to Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
connect.qrLabel: QR code to connect a phone to this PC
connect.url: Or type this address in your phone's browser

steps.title: How to connect
steps.one: Join the same Wi-Fi network on your phone.
steps.two: Scan the QR code with the camera, or type the address.
steps.three: Approve the request on this PC after checking the 4-digit code.

connect.plainHttp: Transfers on your local network use plain HTTP and are not encrypted. Only connect on a network you trust.

warn.no_network: This PC has no active network connection.
warn.address_lost: This PC's network address changed. Regenerate the QR code after reconnecting.
warn.virtual_adapter: The selected network is a virtual adapter, such as a VPN or virtual machine. Phones usually cannot reach it.
warn.not_private_range: The selected address is not in a private range. Your phone may not be on the same network.
warn.multiple_adapters: Several networks are available. If the phone cannot connect, choose a different one.
warn.public_profile: Windows treats this network as Public, which blocks incoming connections unless a rule allows them. This is the most common reason a phone cannot open the page.
warn.better_interface: Veydrop is listening on a different network than the one it would pick now. Switch to the recommended network and use the new QR code.
warn.local_check_failed: Veydrop could not answer a request from this PC itself. The server may be unhealthy; stop and start the connection.
warn.firewall_blocked: A Windows Firewall rule explicitly blocks Veydrop on this network. Block rules override allow rules.
warn.firewall_no_rule: Windows Firewall has no rule allowing incoming connections to Veydrop on this network, so a phone's request is probably dropped.
warn.not_reached: No other device has reached this PC yet. Opening the address on this PC does not count: it never goes through the firewall.

tip.firewall: When Windows Defender Firewall asks, allow Veydrop on private networks. Veydrop does not change firewall settings by itself.
tip.sameWifi: The phone and PC must be on the same Wi-Fi network, not one on mobile data.
tip.guest: Guest Wi-Fi and some public networks isolate devices from each other. Use your main network or a phone hotspot.
tip.vpn: Turn off VPNs on the phone and PC while transferring, or choose the correct network above.

diag.title: Connection diagnostics
diag.intro: Checks what this PC can verify. Only a request from another device proves a phone can connect.
diag.notRun: Not checked yet. Press Run diagnostics to also read the Windows network profile and firewall rules (read-only).
diag.localNote: A request from this PC to its own address never passes the firewall, so success here does not prove a phone can connect.
diag.localOk: Server answered with a valid page ({{ms}} ms)
diag.externalNo: No other device has reached the server yet
diag.externalNote: This is the real test. If you opened the address on your phone and this stays empty, the request is not arriving, which is usually the firewall or the wrong network.

fw.allowed: A rule allows incoming connections to Veydrop
fw.off: Firewall is off for this profile

diag.pairingActive: Code active, waiting to be scanned
diag.fixDesc: Veydrop never changes firewall or network settings. If you want to allow it, open PowerShell as administrator and run this command. It only opens this program's own port range, for this network profile, to devices on your local subnet.
diag.fixAlt: Alternative: set this network to Private in Windows Settings → Network & internet. That is your decision; Veydrop will not do it.
diag.switchDesc: Switch to {{name}} ({{ip}}). The server restarts, the QR code changes and paired phones are disconnected.
diag.switchConfirm: This restarts the connection and disconnects {{n}} paired phone(s). Continue?

pair.title: A phone wants to connect
pair.desc: Make sure the code below matches the one shown on your phone before approving.
pair.warn: Only approve phones that you recognize. Approved phones can send files to this PC and download what you share.

send.title: Send Files
send.subtitle: Choose what to share. Only these items are visible to a connected phone.
send.emptyDesc: Add files or folders, or drag them onto this window.
send.liveHint: Sharing is on. The phone can see and download these items.
send.liveNoPhone: Sharing is on, but no phone is connected.
send.idleHint: Sharing is off. Nothing is visible to phones until you start.

receive.title: Receive Files
receive.subtitle: Files sent from a phone arrive after you accept them.
receive.trustNote: Automatic acceptance is on for trusted phones. Only phones you approved and marked trusted skip this prompt.
receive.emptyRunningDesc: When a phone sends files, the request will appear here for you to accept or reject.
receive.emptyOffDesc: Start a connection to let a phone send files to this PC.

activity.title: Activity
activity.subtitle: Every transfer on this PC, kept locally.
activity.emptyDesc: Finished transfers will be listed here.
activity.clearDesc: This removes the list only. The files you received stay where they were saved.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Preferences are saved automatically.
settings.languageDesc: Interface language. Arabic switches the layout to right-to-left.
settings.themeDesc: Match Windows, or force dark or light.
settings.deviceNameDesc: Shown on your phone while connected.
settings.downloadDirDesc: Where received files are saved by default.
settings.notificationsDesc: Notify about pairing requests, incoming files, and finished transfers.
settings.startupDesc: Start minimized to the tray. The server does not run until you connect.
settings.trayDesc: Closing the window hides Veydrop to the system tray instead of quitting.
settings.askReceiveDesc: Require approval for each incoming batch of files.
settings.trustKnownDesc: Let a phone you approved reconnect without a new code check. Files still need approval if the setting above is on.
settings.pairingSecondsDesc: How long a pairing code stays valid.
settings.sessionMinutesDesc: A phone must pair again after this time.
settings.chunkSizeDesc: Larger chunks are faster on good Wi-Fi; smaller chunks recover faster.
settings.parallelDesc: How many files a phone uploads at once.
settings.maxFileDesc: Reject bigger files. Zero means no limit.
settings.partialRetentionDesc: Incomplete files are deleted after this time.
settings.portDesc: Zero picks a free port automatically.
settings.retentionDesc: Older entries are removed. Zero keeps everything.
settings.clearHistoryDesc: Remove the list of past transfers.
settings.aboutNote: Veydrop works on your local network only. It is not code signed, and transfers over plain HTTP are not encrypted.

close.title: Close Veydrop?
close.serverBody: The connection is active. If you hide Veydrop, the server stays active in the system tray and phones stay connected.
close.trayBody: Veydrop can keep running in the system tray, or quit completely.
close.activeBody: Transfers in progress: {{n}}. If you hide Veydrop they continue in the system tray. Quitting cancels them.
close.quitNote: Quit stops the server, disconnects every phone, and removes unfinished temporary files.

drop.title: Drop to share
drop.desc: Files and folders are added to Send Files.
